proposed_fixes.title: Command Palette tray icon may fail after Windows cumulative update
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Command Palette tray integration or shell registration may not recover after an OS update, leaving the tray command/icon unavailable until the module is toggled.
plan: Trace tray registration and Command Palette activation after a Windows update reboot.
Make registration failure recoverable and ensure the icon is restored after the shell/module restart path.
Add a regression test for tray registration retry after startup failure.
verification: After a supported Windows update reboot, verify the Command Palette tray icon appears without toggling its setting.

confidence.rationale: Shell registration failure may be related, but the missing icon and error could be separate; current reproduction is unconfirmed.

comment.body: Thanks for explaining that the issue only followed Windows update reboots and that updates were unavailable when asked earlier. No need to force a downgrade or change your Windows update channel. When the next applicable update is installed, could you reply with the Windows build and PowerToys version and confirm whether the enabled tray icon disappears or a registration dialog appears? This will establish whether the current startup path still fails.
